target_customer: Robotics companies training and evaluating manipulation policies
problem: Evaluating and training robot policies on real hardware is slow, so teams need high fidelity simulation and RL environments.
business_model: Simulation and RL environment platform, usage based

competitors.name: Antioch
competitors.what: Simulation tools for robotics, 'Cursor for physical AI'

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a simulation from a few teleoperation episodes with small sim to real gap is research heavy.

defensibility.rationale: Well funded competitors and NVIDIA tooling; quality of world models is the only moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competing platforms raised larger rounds in 2026; no incumbent action against Fern found.

market_need_then: Robotics teams adopting RL and evals created funding for simulation startups in 2026.

branding.name_origin: Company previously named Ishiki Labs; reason for the rename to Fern not stated
branding.domain_note: fern.bot domain; legal entity Ishiki Labs, Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short and direct, 'Enabling physical AI at scale'

rebrands.why: Not stated; accompanied by a pivot to robotics (exact date not given)

brand_strength.rationale: Short friendly name and .bot domain fit robotics; little brand evidence and a name shared with other companies named Fern.

pivots.from: Socially aware AI meeting assistant with real time sales coaching (Ishiki Labs)
pivots.to: Custom robot world models and simulation for RL policy training (Fern)

outcome_analysis: Fern, formerly Ishiki Labs, pivoted within the Winter 2026 YC batch from meeting AI to robotics simulation and reports customers ran 900k rollouts. No funding is verified. It competes with larger funded simulation startups and NVIDIA, so the pivot's success is not yet proven.
notes: No funding found; search results for funding named other companies. The 900k rollouts figure is a company claim. Which founder holds the Purdue PhD is stated for the CEO on the YC page. Robert Xu education not found.
